claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a nominally homogeneous elemental distribution.
Pre-annealing at approximately 650°C promotes Cu segregation to the coating surface.
The proposed annealing treatment forms a continuous Cu-rich surface layer.
The near-surface Cu-rich structure may instead occur as a nanophase.
Elevated temperature increases atomic mobility in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Increased atomic mobility drives Cu diffusion and segregation from the coating bulk to the surface.
A Cu-rich surface layer provides a lubricious sliding interface.
The Cu-rich layer lowers friction during high-temperature sliding.
The Cu-rich layer stabilizes the near-surface microstructure against plastic deformation during sliding.
The Cu-rich layer improves the coating's high-temperature wear resistance.
Pre-annealed coatings will have smaller wear-track dimensions than as-deposited coatings during high-temperature sliding.
Pre-annealed coatings will have lower friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings during high-temperature sliding.
Pre-annealed coatings will exhibit less microscopic deformation than as-deposited coatings during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted segregation-mediated wear benefit is expected to hold at sliding temperatures above 600°C.
The proposed mechanism may not operate at lower temperatures because thermal activation may be insufficient to drive Cu segregation.
